# E0303: orphan impl

An impl of a trait lives in the trait's module or the type's module, so that a type never gets two impls of one trait from two places. Move it to one of them.

- Rule: [`traits.orphan-rule`](../../reference/11-traits.md#traits.orphan-rule)
- Reported at: the impl's `impl` keyword.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `items` phase

## What the compiler prints

The program [`E0303_orphan_impl`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0303_orphan_impl):

`main.lt`:

```stilt fragment
use names
use things

impl names.Named for things.Thing {
  fn name(self) -> str { "thing" }
}
```

`names.lt`:

```stilt fragment
pub trait Named {
  fn name(self) -> str
}
```

`things.lt`:

```stilt fragment
pub type Thing = {}
```

What `stilt check` prints for it:

```text
── ORPHAN IMPL ──────────────────────────────────────────── main.lt:4:1  [E0303]

An impl of `Named` for `Thing` must be in module `names` or `things`:

  4 │ impl names.Named for things.Thing {
    │ ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

An impl of a trait lives in the trait's module or the type's module, so that a
type never gets two impls of one trait from two places. Move it to one of them.
```
